olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Do there exist positive integers $x_1,\ldots,x_{1985}$ (distinct) satisfying $x_1^2+\cdots+x_{1985}^2=y^3$ and $x_1^3+\cdots+x_{1985}^3=z^2$ simultaneously?
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1985

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Determine each real root of $x^4-(2\cdot10^{10}+1)x^2-x+10^{20}+10^{10}-1=0$ correct to four decimal places.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1985

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $A,B,C,D$ are distinct points with at most one of $AB,AC,AD,BC,BD,CD$ greater than 1. Determine the maximum value of the sum of the six distances.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1985

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: There are $n$ people at a party. Prove there are two people such that of the remaining $n-2$, at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1$ of them either know both or know neither of the two.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1985

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $a_1\leq a_2\leq\cdots$ be a nondecreasing sequence of positive integers. Define $b_m=\min\{n:a_n\geq m\}$. If $a_{19}=85$, find the maximum of $a_1+\cdots+a_{19}+b_1+\cdots+b_{85}$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1985
